canonical_name: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents (Wei et al., OpenAI)
release_source: https://openai.com/index/browsecomp/ (blog dated April 10, 2025); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12516 v1 2025-04-16; data/grader in github.com/openai/simple-evals
metric: accuracy (% of 1,266 questions whose short answer matches the reference, LLM-graded), agent with browsing tools
ab_mode: pass@1 single run per question, browsing + tools ('Tool use' table); Pro tier = parallel test-time compute inside the product
ab_source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/ (2026-04-23; table row 'BrowseComp 84.4% | 82.7% | 90.1% | 89.3% | 79.3% | 85.9%' for GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.5 Pro / GPT-5.4 Pro / Claude Opus 4.7 / Gemini 3.1 Pro)
score_at_release_system: OpenAI Deep Research (paper Table 3 / blog; o1 9.9, GPT-4o w/ browsing 1.9); Deep Research best-of-64 aggregation ~75
lineage: No parent. Derivatives by other teams: BrowseComp-ZH (arXiv 2504.19314, 2025-04), BrowseComp-Plus fixed-corpus version (arXiv 2508.06600, 2025-08), multimodal BrowseComp-VL/MM-BrowseComp. OpenAI's 'BrowseComp Long Context 128k/256k' (GPT-5 developer post 2025-08) is a different long-context eval, not this unit.
best_by_cutoff: 93.3 — Claude Mythos 5 multi-agent (Anthropic system card 2026-06-09, per batch lab_reports; single-agent 88.0; PDF too long to verify). Verified by me: Atria Dawn Preview 92.5 (Shanghai AI Lab, released 2026-09-11, llm-stats.com/benchmarks/browsecomp), GPT-6 Astra 91.5 (openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra, 2026-09), Kimi K3 91.2 (2026-07-16).
notes: Human trainers solved only 29.2% (gave up on 70.8%; 86.4% agreement with reference when solved) -> criterion B, threshold 90. Trajectory before the event: Deep Research 51.5 (2025-04) -> ChatGPT agent 68.9 (2025-07) -> Claude Opus 4.6 single 83.7 / multi-agent 86.6 (2026-02-05) -> Gemini 3.1 Pro 85.9 (2026-02-19) -> GPT-5.4 Pro 89.3 (2026-03-05) -> Claude Mythos Preview 86.9 (2026-04-07) -> Kimi K2.6 Agent Swarm 86.3 (2026-04) -> GPT-5.5 Pro 90.1 (2026-04-23, first >=90 found). Later >=90: Claude Mythos 5 multi-agent 93.3 (2026-06-09), GPT-5.6 Sol 90.4 (2026-07-09), Kimi K3 91.2, Claude Opus 5 90.8, Gemini 3.8 Flash 90.8 (per GPT-6 Astra table). 'BrowseComp Long Context 128k' 90-92% results by GPT-5/5.1/5.2 (2025-08 to 2025-12) are a different eval and were NOT counted. Strict event: none — no organizer leaderboard and no independent run >=90 found; OpenAI is both creator and model developer, so its own-model results were not treated as organizer verification (same rule as Graphwalks). Contamination: Anthropic engineering post 'Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6's BrowseComp performance' (2026-03-06) found 11/1,266 problems answered from leaked benchmark materials (incl. the model decrypting the canary-XOR answer key from GitHub) — <1% of items, not coded as E; Anthropic adopted blocklists. simple-evals repo deprecation notice (July 2025) keeps BrowseComp reference implementation, not a C event. Search for earlier non-lab >=90 claims (agent startups) limited to llm-stats aggregator (67 models) since WebSearch unavailable.

canonical_name: BrowseComp-ZH: Benchmarking Web Browsing Ability of Large Language Models in Chinese (Zhou et al., 2025)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19314 (v1 2025-04-27); GitHub github.com/PALIN2018/BrowseComp-ZH initial commit 2025-04-24, encrypted data 'v0' 2025-04-28
metric: accuracy (% of 289 questions answered correctly; GPT-4o answer extraction vs reference); calibration error secondary
score_at_release_system: OpenAI DeepResearch (paper Table 1 / README; next o1 29.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro 27.3)
lineage: Parent/inspiration: BrowseComp (OpenAI, 2025-04; different team) — Chinese-native multi-hop browsing questions across 11 domains. No successor version by the same authors found by cutoff.
best_by_cutoff: 81.3 — ByteDance Seed 1.8 (model card Table 4, Pass@1; arXiv submit 2025-12-17, github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Seed-1.8 'init' 2025-12-19; the card's text says 78.5). Best among the 9 labs: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 70.3 (2026-02-16); llm-stats.com/benchmarks/browsecomp-zh lists 15 models, max 81.3.
notes: Paper reports no human solve rate (annotators only used a 10-minute limit to filter out easily findable questions) -> criterion B, threshold 90. Lab trajectory: DeepSeek-V3.1 49.2 (2025-08-21), Grok 4 Fast 51.2 (2025-09-19), Kimi K2 Thinking 62.3 avg@4 (2025-11-06), DeepSeek-V3.2 65.0 (2025-12-01), Qwen3.5 70.3 (2026-02-16; last lab report found). No result >=90 found by 2026-09-30. GitHub leaderboard static since 2025-05 (last commit 2025-05-14); labs reported it until 2026-02 (<12 months before cutoff), so not abandoned. Search limited (no WebSearch; Qwen blog JS-rendered and unreadable); Chinese deep-research agents may have unreported higher scores, but none near 90 surfaced on llm-stats.

canonical_name: CVE-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents' Ability to Exploit Real-World Web Application Vulnerabilities (Zhu et al., UIUC Kang lab; ICML 2025)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17332 (v1 2025-03-21); repo github.com/uiuc-kang-lab/cve-bench README news '[2025-03-31] CVE-Bench released with 40 critical severity tasks' (initial commit is author-dated 2024-06-29 but the repo was not public before the paper)
metric: success rate (% of the 40 critical CVEs successfully exploited per the automatic grader), zero-day and one-day prompt settings; paper reports success with 1 attempt and with 5 attempts (success@5)
score_at_release_system: T-Agent (teams of GPT-4o agents), one-day setting, success@5 (zero-day best 10%, T-Agent/AutoGPT; Cy-Agent 2.5%)
n_items: 40 CVEs (each with zero-day and one-day variants)
lineage: v1.0 (2025-03, 40 critical web-app CVEs) -> v2.0.0 (2025-10-30, grader/validity fixes on ~16 tasks guided by the Agentic Benchmark Checklist; ddkang.substack.com post) -> v2.1.0 (2026-01-12, 'Arbitrary file upload is no longer an evaluation criterion, and has been replaced with Remote code execution') -> 2.2.0 (repo 2026-09-24). Related: Cybench (CTF, 2024-08).
best_by_cutoff: No full 40-task result >=90 found. Highest documented: GPT-5.3-Codex 90% on OpenAI's 34-of-40 subset, zero-day, pass@1 over 3 rollouts (GPT-5.3-Codex system card, 2026-02-05; GPT-5.2-Codex 87%); GPT-5.4 Thinking 86.27% same subset (2026-03-05); later OpenAI cards (GPT-5.5/5.6) give values only in figures. xAI Grok 4.6 39.8% 'reward' (model card 2026-08-12).
notes: No human baseline (reference exploits by experts took 5-24 person-hours each; validation only) -> criterion B, threshold 90. KEY JUDGEMENT: OpenAI system cards (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max 2025-11-18 onward) run CVE-Bench v1.0 on only 34 of the 40 challenges ('due to some infrastructure challenges porting the eval, we only ran 34 out of the 40 benchmark challenges'), zero-day prompt, pass@1 over 3 rollouts. GPT-5.3-Codex reached 90% on that subset (2026-02-05), but a subset is not the official test split (90% of 34 tasks = 76.5% of 40 if the rest fail), so NOT counted; sensitivity: if subset results were accepted, AB = 2026-02 (GPT-5.3-Codex 90%, self). xAI reports much lower 'reward' values (Grok 4.6 39.8%, Grok 4.7 36.6%), likely on a newer version/grader. Versions v2.0/v2.1 changed graders and one criterion (protocol change); treated as the same unit here because labs report under one name. No official leaderboard in the repo; the v2.0 fixes are maintenance, not a C event. Still reported in 2026-08/09 -> alive.

canonical_name: Claw-Eval: Towards Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents (Ye et al., PKU/HKU, 2026)
release_source: Leaderboard site repo github.com/claw-eval/claw-eval.github.io 'Deploy webpage' + 'update new results' 2026-03-12 (104 tasks with per-task cases); code/tasks repo github.com/claw-eval/claw-eval 'release v1.0.0' 2026-03-18; arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06132 v1 2026-04-07
metric: Pass^3 (% of tasks passed in all 3 independent trials; rubric-based full-trajectory grading of completion/safety/robustness, LLM grader gemini-3-flash, Claude Opus 4.6 for multi-turn); secondary: average score, pass@3
score_at_release_system: Claude Opus 4.6 (launch leaderboard 2026-03-12, single-trial pass rate on 104 tasks, avg score 0.759); first Pass^3 board 2026-03-17: Opus 4.6 66.3
n_items: 300 in v1.1 (161 general + 101 multimodal + 38 multi-turn; 2,159 rubric items); v1.0 had 104 general tasks
lineage: v0.0.0 (2026-03) -> v1.0.0 (2026-03-18, 104 tasks; Pass^3 adopted 2026-03-17) -> v1.1.0 (2026-04-09, 300 tasks in general/multimodal/multi-turn splits; multimodal split reported by Qwen as 'ClawEval-MM'). Tasks adapted from OpenClaw, PinchBench, OfficeQA, OneMillion-Bench, Finance Agent and Terminal-Bench 2.0. EvalScope integration 2026-07-24.
best_by_cutoff: Pass^3 70.4 overall / 70.8 general — Claude Opus 4.6 (official leaderboard data, last site deploy 2026-06-29, claw-eval.github.io). Lab self-reports: Kimi K2.6 pass^3 62.3 / pass@3 80.9 (2026-04); Qwen3.8-Max ClawEval-MM pass@3 77.2 / avg 74.8 (2026-08-03). Highest pass@3 on board 83.9 (Step 3.7 Flash).
notes: Primary metric per README: 'Primary Metric: Pass^3' (strict all-3-trials). No human baseline -> criterion B, threshold 90. No result >=90 on any of Pass^3, pass@3 or avg score by cutoff (leaderboard data extracted from the site's JS bundles in the git history). The task set grew from 104 (v1.0) to 300 (v1.1), which by the codebook would justify separate units; coded as one unit because labs report under one name and both versions are far below threshold. Leaderboard updates paused after 2026-06-29 but labs still reported in 2026-08 -> alive.

exclusion_reason: Privately developed scenario suite by the evaluation firm Irregular; no public items, paper or leaderboard. Labs report it only as a third-party/private evaluation (Meta Muse Spark safety and preparedness report: 'privately developed challenges from Irregular'; Anthropic Opus 5 card: 'private novel scenarios').
release_source: https://ai.meta.com/static-resource/muse-spark-safety-and-preparedness-report/ (describes it as privately developed by Irregular, 2025)
lineage: Part of Irregular's private evaluation suite reported alongside other Irregular evals in lab system cards (OpenAI GPT-5.6 card groups it with FrontierCyber and atomic challenges).
notes: Excluded as internal/private: no public dataset, paper or leaderboard found; only lab system cards report it as an external third-party evaluation. Lab reports exist from Meta (2026-04, 2026-07), Anthropic (2026-06 to 2026-09) and OpenAI (2026-07).

canonical_name: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models (Zhang et al., Stanford; ICLR 2025)
metric: end-to-end (unguided) success rate = % of the 40 CTF tasks whose flag is captured; CTF flags are self-verifying. Labs report avg pass@1 and pass@k (pass@10/pass@30)
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet agent (end-to-end % solved on 40 tasks; paper/leaderboard; GPT-4o 12.5, o1-preview 10)
lineage: Parent: selected from 4 professional CTF competitions (HackTheBox, SekaiCTF, Glacier, HKCert). Successor by overlapping Stanford authors: BountyBench (real-world vuln bounties, 2025-06; linked from the Cybench site as 'an all-new, real-world' benchmark, but it does not cite Cybench saturation as the reason, so not coded C).
best_by_cutoff: Full 40-task: Muse Spark 1.1 pass@1 92.9% / pass@10 97.0% (2026-07-09). Subset results on the official leaderboard: Claude Mythos Preview 100% (35-problem subset, avg pass@1, 2026-04-07), Claude Opus 4.7 96% (35-subset, 2026-04-16), Claude Opus 4.6 93% (37-subset, 2026-02-05). Independent HAL leaderboard tops at 25% (o3-mini, 2025-01).
notes: No human success-rate baseline on the same split (the paper's human reference is first-solve-time by competition teams, degenerate for accuracy) -> criterion B, threshold 90. First-by-time VALID full-split crossing = Muse Spark 1.1 92.9% pass@1 on the full 40 (2026-07-09). Earlier >=90 results exist but only on 35/37-problem SUBSETS (Opus 4.6 93% on 37, 2026-02-05; Mythos Preview 100% on 35, 2026-04-07) and a 93% of 37 does not guarantee >=90% of 40, so not counted as the full-split crossing (same subset rule applied to CVE-Bench); sensitivity: if subset leaderboard results count, AB = 2026-02. Strict event left blank: all >=90 results are lab self-reports; the independent HAL leaderboard tops at 25% and the HAL o3-mini/o1-mini numbers are flagged by the maintainers as inflated by a framework answer leak ('likely ran on a fork of the Inspect framework that leaked the answer'). No C: Anthropic's Opus 4.6 card declares '~100% on Cybench (pass@30)... saturated all of our current cyber evaluations' but Anthropic is not the maintainer; the Cybench team's own site still updates (last leaderboard commit 2026-04-16) and only points to BountyBench without citing saturation. Tool use is part of the task, so counted. Leaderboard still active <12 months before cutoff -> not abandoned.
